plan_a_advantages: Includes threshold and tempo work for speed development.
Longer runs specifically target trail endurance.
More structured approach to training, providing a clearer progression.
plan_b_advantages: More trail-based runs in the initial week.
Incorporates a strength session, which can be beneficial for trail running.
Potentially less taxing on the body due to the emphasis on recovery.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates structured workouts like threshold runs and tempo sessions, which are crucial for improving running economy and lactate threshold – key determinants of speed. Plan B, conversely, focuses almost entirely on recovery and relatively short, easy runs with a single hill session, which while important for overall fitness, doesn't provide the targeted stimulus needed for significant speed gains. Plan A’s longer runs at controlled effort also better mimic the demands of trail races, building the necessary endurance.
